review_candidates.title: Senior Technical Lead - HRH Development and Regulation
review_candidates.description: Overview Re-Advertized The Senior Technical Lead – Human Resources for Health (HRH) Development & Regulation provides strategic leadership, technical oversight, and quality assurance for the project's Health Workforce Development and Professional Regulation portfolio under RISE and ASCEND HRH activities The position leads implementation of interventions that strengthen the production, competency, regulation, certification, and continuous professional development of Ethiopia's health workforce while ensuring that national institutions develop sustainable systems capable of continuously improving workforce quality beyond the life of the project. The project supports the Government of Ethiopia to strengthen Human Resources for Health (HRH) systems, particularly in underserved and fragile settings where shortages of competent health workers, limited institutional capacity, and weak regulatory systems continue to affect access to quality primary health care. Working through national institutions and decentralized implementation platforms, the project advances sustainable, country-led HRH reforms that improve workforce competency, performance, resilience, and health system effectiveness. Working closely with the Ministry of Health (MoH), Ministry of Education (MoE), Educational and Training Authority (ETA), Health Professionals Licensing Lead Executive Office (LEO), higher education institutions (HEIs), professional associations (PAs), teaching hospitals, regulatory agencies, and development partners, the Senior Technical Lead provides strategic direction across the education-to-practice continuum, including competency-based pre-service education, educational quality assurance, accreditation, faculty development, simulation-based education, continuing professional development (CPD), competency assessment, national licensing examinations, professional licensing, certification, and professional regulation. Ensure all technical approaches are evidence-based, implementation-oriented, and responsive to Ethiopia's evolving HRH priorities. Guide annual technical planning, priority setting, resource allocation, and implementation sequencing across the project. Provide high-level technical assistance to national institutions in strengthening policies, standards, implementation frameworks, operational guidelines, and institutional systems. Lead or contribute to national technical working groups, advisory committees, policy dialogues, and strategic planning processes. Cultivate and maintain productive working relationships with government counterparts and development partners to promote harmonization, institutional ownership, and sustainability. Ensure project investments strengthen—not duplicate—existing national systems and government priorities. Technical Quality Assurance Ensure all technical interventions meet national standards, international best practices, and donor expectations. Lead quality assurance for development and review of national educational guidelines, standard operating procedures, competency frameworks, competency/outcome-based curricula, accreditation program standards, assessment blueprints, workplace-based assessment tools, licensing procedures, simulation packages, digital learning resources, and technical manuals. Review and approve major technical deliverables before dissemination. Ensure interventions remain technically sound, operationally feasible, and responsive to emerging national priorities. Monitor emerging global evidence and identify innovations appropriate for adaptation within Ethiopia. Promote implementation science and continuous improvement across technical interventions. Institutional Capacity Strengthening and Technical Mentorship Strengthen institutional capacity of government agencies, higher education institutions, regulatory bodies, professional associations, and teaching hospitals to independently sustain HRH reforms. Provide high-level technical mentoring and coaching to Senior Advisors, Subnational Technical Team, government counterparts, and partner organizations. Support development of national technical expertise and succession planning. Foster multidisciplinary collaboration and strengthen communities of practice that promote continuous learning and technical excellence. Promote integrated implementation approaches that strengthen institutional systems rather than isolated interventions. Ensure interventions contribute to sustainable health systems strengthening and long-term government ownership. Identify implementation successes, challenges, risks, bottlenecks, and emerging opportunities. Recommend corrective actions and technical adaptations that improve program effectiveness. Support adaptive management through regular technical reviews, learning sessions, after-action reviews, and performance reflection meetings. Work closely with the MEL team to strengthen evidence generation and utilization for continuous improvement. Promote documentation and dissemination of innovations, lessons learned, and best practices nationally and internationally. Foster organizational learning and strengthen technical communities of practice across project partners. Identify opportunities for strategic partnerships, leveraged investments, and future HRH programming. Experience reviewing imaging protocols, technical quality records, and radiology department audit documentation. Opportunity to contribute to diagnostic imaging quality and radiology service improvement. Collaboration with radiologists, radiographers, medical physicists, and healthcare quality professionals. Exposure to modern imaging technologies and digital radiology systems. Opportunities for professional development in medical imaging quality assurance and technical coordination. How to Apply Interested candidates should submit an updated CV highlighting their radiography experience, imaging modality expertise, quality assurance knowledge, radiation safety training, and relevant professional registration or licensing. Application Subject: Application – Senior Radiographer (UAE Remote) Candidates should confirm applicable employment arrangements, residency requirements, and work authorization before accepting an offer. Physical patient positioning, imaging examinations, scan acquisition, equipment operation, radiation exposure procedures, and direct patient care must be performed by appropriately qualified and locally authorized radiography personnel. Diagnostic interpretation, clinical decisions, patient management, regulated clinical reporting, and formal professional sign-offs must be completed by appropriately licensed healthcare professionals.

Access to your own laptop, a quiet workspace and strong internet. Start date: First week of January. Flexibility can be discussed. Compensation: in line with market rates and will vary depending on experience level. Exact numbers will be discussed with the founder following the video interview.
